claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits extensive primary crystallization involving multiple primary non-eutectic phases.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 undergoes a multistep crystallization sequence during cooling and reheating.
Conventional melt spinning produces relatively low amorphous retention in this alloy.
Primary non-eutectic phase formation reduces the alloy's thermal stability upon reheating.
Increasing melt-spinning wheel speed or equivalent quenching intensity increases the effective cooling rate.
Cooling rates above 10^6 K/s, or otherwise above conventional practice, constitute the proposed ultra-rapid-quenching regime.
Ultra-rapid quenching reduces the number of crystalline embryos nucleated in the alloy.
Ultra-rapid quenching reduces the size of crystalline embryos in the alloy.
Reducing crystalline embryo number and size produces a predominantly amorphous matrix.
Sharply increasing the cooling rate kinetically limits atomic mobility.
Limited atomic mobility suppresses diffusion required for nucleation and growth of primary non-eutectic phases.
Suppression of nucleation and growth traps a larger fraction of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 in an amorphous state.
Ultra-rapidly quenched material will have a higher amorphous volume fraction than conventionally melt-spun material.
Ultra-rapidly quenched material will exhibit a higher crystallization-onset temperature during reheating than the control.
The intervention is effective only when cooling exceeds a critical rate that suppresses diffusion-mediated crystallization.
